To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) participants’ emotional ratings to visual, auditory, and haptic stimuli are different; 2) participants’ skin conductance responses to visual, auditory or haptic stimuli are also different; 3) participants’ emotional rating to visual, auditory stimuli are correlated to the skin conductance response, whereas the correlation between emotional ratings and skin conductances response to haptic stimuli are lower.
the emotional ratings to visual, auditory, and haptic stimuli were significantly correlated (p<.01), but the physiological reactions (i. e., skin conductance) were not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emotional reactions to stimuli from different modalities in the same person.
the comparison of the emotional reactions to stimuli of different modalities in the same individual.

the emotional reactions to stimuli eliciting different types of emotions (fear, anger, happiness) through different sensory modalities (visual, auditory, haptic) and the physiological reactions of the participants to such stimuli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) the type of stimuli (visual, auditory, or somatosensory) influences the emotional state of a participant, 2) there is a correlation between the emotional state of the participant and the skin conductance response of the participant, 3) there is no difference between the skin conductance of participants in the different emotional states, 4) there is no correlation between the emotional rating and the skin conductances in the different emotional categories.
the emotional ratings of the stimuli delivered by different modalities are not significantly different.
there are no significant differences in the emotional reaction of participants when exposed to the same stimulus delivered through different modalities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide an open database of emotional stimuli, their emotional rating, and their physiological reactions, in a within participant design.
the emotional reaction to stimuli of different sensory modalities are not significantly different.
, in general, participants’ emotional reactions to stimuli are not modality-dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we provide a dataset where the same participant is tested with different stimuli, allowing for the comparison of different types of stimuli within the same participant, and the possibility to compare results obtained with different stimuli in a within-participant experimental design.
, for the first time, the emotional reactions to stimuli from the same participants delivered through different modalities are available in the same dataset.
we provide a database with emotional ratings and skin conductances from the same participants for stimuli delivered via different sensory modalities.
